p: holy brethren: Having laid the foundation that is to say, declared and proved both the natures of one Christ, he gives him three offices, that is, the office of a Prophet, King and Priest, and concerning the office of teaching, and governing, compares him with Moses and Joshua from Heb 3:1-4:14, and with Aaron concerning the priesthood. He proposes that which he intends to speak of, with a grave exhortation, that all our faith may be directed towards Christ, as the only everlasting teacher, governor, and High Priest.
Apostle and High Priest of our: The ambassador or messenger, as in Ro 15:8 he is called the minister of circumcision.
profession: Of the doctrine of the gospel which we profess.

Who was faithful to him that: He confirms his exhortation with two reasons, first of all because Christ Jesus was appointed as such by God: secondly, because he thoroughly executed the offices that his Father commanded him.
appointed him: Apostle and High Priest.

as also Moses was faithful in: Now he comes to the comparison with Moses, and he makes them like one another other in this, that they were both appointed rulers over God's house, and executed faithfully their office: but he later shows that there is great dissimilarity in the same comparison.

For this man was counted worthy: The first comparison: The builder of the house is better than the house itself, therefore Christ is better than Moses. The reason for the conclusion is this: because the builder of the house is God, which cannot be attributed to Moses; and therefore Moses was not the builder, but a part of the house: but Christ as Lord and God, made the house.

Moses verily was faithful in all: Another comparison: Moses was a faithful servant in this house, that is, in the Church, serving the Lord that was to come, but Christ rules and governs his house as Lord.

whose: He applies the former doctrine to his purpose, exhorting all men by the words of David to hear the Son speak, and to give full credit to his words, seeing that otherwise they cannot enter into that eternal rest.
house are we: That is, Christ's.
confidence and the rejoicing of the: He calls confidence the excellent effect of faith (by which we cry Abba, that is, Father), and to confidence he adds hope.
will hear his voice: So that God was to speak once again after Moses.
provocation: In the day that they troubled the Lord, or struggled with him.
err in their heart: They are brutish and angry.

Take heed: Now consider in the words of David, he shows first by this word "today" that we must not ignore the opportunity while we have it: for that word is not to be limited to David's time, but it encompasses all the time in which God calls us.
while it is called To day: While today lasts, that is to say, so long as the gospel is offered to us.

For we are made partakers of: Now he considers these words, "If you hear his voice" showing that they are spoken and meant of the hearing of faith, opposite which he places hardening through unbelief.
beginning of our confidence stedfast unto: That beginning of trust and confidence: in the speech of the Hebrews, he calls "beginning" that which is chiefest.
While it is said: So long as this voice sounds out.
